claim: EvoPrompting's naive few-shot prompting baseline (single round, T=1, no evolutionary feedback loop) fails to design competitive architectures, while adding evolutionary selection and prompt-tuning across rounds substantially improves results.
stance_target: the target paper's thesis that iterative feedback degrades LLM-guided NAS proposals
scope_conditions: 62B-parameter PaLM code model on MNIST-1D CNN search and CLRS GNN search; not a small/quantised model
quoted_support: It is also evident from both Figure 2(a) and 2(b) that performance suffers when any individual component is removed. Interestingly, Figure 2(a) indicates that prompting with randomly selected parents combined with prompt-tuning is no more effective than naive prompting alone.

claim: The EvoPrompting random-parents ablation (removing fitness-based selection/feedback while keeping prompt-tuning) plateaus fastest and at the worst fitness of any tested variant, showing that removing feedback-driven selection hurts search rather than helps it.
stance_target: the target paper's thesis that feedback degrades proposals
quoted_support: The random parents baseline plateaus the quickest, reaching a maximum fitness by the time approximately 200 individuals have been generated. Furthermore, the maximum fitness it reaches is significantly worse than that of the other experiments.

claim: EvoPrompting explicitly attributes output diversity to mixed-temperature sampling (uniform over T in {0.2, 0.6, 0.8, 1.0}) rather than relying on a single fixed decoding temperature, and reports the method 'consistently finds diverse and high performing models,' contrasting with a single-template-collapse outcome.
stance_target: the claim that LLM-guided architecture proposal inherently collapses to a single template
quoted_support: We always sample from πθ₀ with mixed temperature sampling, in which the sampling temperature is selected uniformly from [0.2, 0.6, 0.8, 1.0].

claim: EvoPrompting's authors self-identify a methodological limitation: they lack an extensive comparison against standard NAS techniques on a shared tabular benchmark, and their one NATS-Bench comparison handicaps EvoPrompting by removing its code-pretraining advantage and by pulling competitor accuracy numbers from a different paper (Dong et al. 2021) rather than re-running them under matched conditions.
stance_target: methodology standards for LLM-NAS papers using tabular benchmarks
quoted_support: We make a brief comparison of EvoPrompting against other NAS algorithms on the NATS-Bench Size Search Space (Dong et al. 2021). However, we note that this comparison is limited because it handicaps EvoPrompting in multiple ways.

claim: EvoPrompting discovered GNN architectures that outperform the prior state-of-the-art Triplet-GMPNN on 21 of 30 CLRS Algorithmic Reasoning Benchmark tasks while maintaining similar model size.
stance_target: capability ceiling of LLM-guided architecture search when combined with evolutionary feedback
scope_conditions: CLRS Algorithmic Reasoning Benchmark, 30 classical algorithms
quoted_support: EvoPrompting generates novel architectures that outperform state-of-the-art models on 21 out of 30 algorithmic reasoning tasks (Appendix 3).
numbers: 125.19% OOD accuracy increase for ConcatRep on heapsort with 6.68% model size increase
